code:
module serializer(
    input wire clk,
    input wire start,
    input wire enable,
    input wire [31:0] data_in,
    output reg serial_out,
    output reg done
);
    reg [5:0] bit_counter; // 6 bits to count from 0 to 31
    reg [31:0] shift_reg;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (start) begin
            bit_counter <= 0;
            shift_reg <= data_in;
            done <= 0;
        end else if (enable) begin
            if (bit_counter < 32) begin
                serial_out <= shift_reg[31]; // Output the MSB
                shift_reg <= shift_reg << 1; // Shift left to move next bit to MSB
                bit_counter <= bit_counter + 1;
            end else begin
                serial_out <= 0; // No more bits to serialize
                done <= 1; // Serialization is done
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a SPI master controller in Verilog that can send and receive data serially. The SPI master should have the following functionalities:
1. It should be able to initiate communication.
2. It should send a byte of data and receive a byte of data from the slave.
3. The clock should be generated at a specified frequency.
4. It should have a signal to indicate when the transmission is complete.
code:
module spi_master (
    input wire clk,               // system clock
    input wire reset,             // reset signal
    input wire [7:0] data_in,     // data input to send
    input wire start,             // start signal
    output reg mosi,              // master out, slave in
    output reg sck,               // serial clock
    input wire miso,              // master in, slave out
    output reg cs,                // chip select
    output reg done               // done signal
);
    
    reg [3:0] bit_count;          // count the bits
    reg [7:0] data_out;           // data register
    reg sending;                  // flag to indicate sending process

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            mosi <= 0;
            sck <= 0;
            cs <= 1;               // chip select inactive
            done <= 0;
            bit_count <= 0;
            sending <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (start && !sending) begin
                cs <= 0;           // activate chip select
                data_out <= data_in;
                bit_count <= 8;    // start sending 8 bits
                sending <= 1;      
                done <= 0;         
            end
            
            if (sending) begin
                if (bit_count > 0) begin
                    sck <= ~sck;     // toggle clock
                    if (sck) begin
                        mosi <= data_out[bit_count-1]; // send bit
                    end else begin
                        data_out[bit_count-1] <= miso; // receive bit
                        bit_count <= bit_count - 1; // decrease count
                    end
                end else begin
                    sending <= 0;      // done sending
                    cs <= 1;           // deactivate chip select
                    done <= 1;         // signal done
                end
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

code:
module booth_multiplier (
    input signed [3:0] A,
    input signed [3:0] B,
    output reg signed [7:0] P
);
    reg signed [7:0] M;
    reg signed [7:0] Q;
    reg Q_1; // Previous least significant bit of Q
    integer i;

    always @(*) begin
        M = {4'b0000, A}; // Extend A to 8 bits
        Q = {4'b0000, B}; // Extend B to 8 bits
        Q_1 = 0;          // Initialize Q_1 to 0
        P = 0;           // Initialize product to 0

        for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
            case ({Q[0], Q_1})
                2'b01: P = P + M;      // Add M to P
                2'b10: P = P - M;      // Subtract M from P
            endcase
            
            // Arithmetic right shift
            {P, Q} = {P[7], P, Q[7:1]};
            Q_1 = Q[0]; // Update Q_1 to current Q[0]
        end
    end
endmodule
